contests.primaryCanceledReason: All three party primaries canceled — only one candidate filed per party, so no ballot appearance was needed.
contests.districtNotes: Covers most of Wake County, including Raleigh. Cook PVI of D+17 makes this the 77th most Democratic district nationally. Ross has won her past three elections with 60%+ of the vote.

candidates.background: Attorney and three-term U.S. Representative for NC-02 since January 2021. Prior to Congress, served 10 years in the North Carolina House of Representatives (District 34, 2003–2013). Earlier career as civil rights attorney and state director for the ACLU of North Carolina (1994–). Education: B.A. International Relations, Brown University (1985); J.D., UNC Chapel Hill School of Law (1990). Born 1963 in Philadelphia, PA.
committees: House Judiciary Committee (including Courts/IP/AI and Immigration subcommittees)
House Science, Space, and Technology Committee (Energy and Environment subcommittees)
candidates.notes: Incumbent with three full terms of voting record available. Extensive committee assignments and press coverage. Well-funded with over $1.1M cash on hand. Filed for re-election December 6, 2025.

candidates.background: Retired chemistry professor and education consultant based in Raleigh, NC. Over 30 years of teaching experience in chemistry. Education: B.S., The King's College (1979); M.S., University of Connecticut (1982); Ph.D. Chemistry, North Carolina State University (2010). Affiliated with the American Chemistry Society. Baptist Christian. Previously ran for U.S. House NC-02 in 2024, placing second in the Republican primary with 22.5% of the vote (9,751 votes) behind Alan Swain.
statedPositions: Smaller federal government, less regulation, lower taxes
Elimination of the Department of Education
Strict opposition to abortion from conception
Opposition to gender-affirming care for minors

withdrawnCandidates.withdrawalStage: before primary — Democratic primary subsequently canceled
withdrawnCandidates.background: Limited public profile. Social media presence on Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, and TikTok. Campaign raised only $529 total before withdrawal.
withdrawnCandidates.notes: Filed for Democratic primary then withdrew before the March 3, 2026 filing-based cutoff. His withdrawal left Ross as the only Democrat filed, causing the primary cancellation. Reason for withdrawal not publicly stated.

ballotMeasures.originatingBody: North Carolina State Legislature (passed with required 60% supermajority in each chamber, December 2024)
ballotMeasures.yesVoteMeans: Amends the North Carolina Constitution to require photographic identification for all voters regardless of voting method (in-person, absentee, etc.)
ballotMeasures.noVoteMeans: Maintains current voting identification procedures; existing photo ID requirements would remain without constitutional mandate extension to all voting methods
ballotMeasures.policyContext: North Carolina has had an in-person voter ID law since 2019. This amendment would extend a constitutional photo ID requirement to absentee and all other voting methods, closing a gap that currently exists in the constitutional mandate.
ballotMeasures.notes: Only statewide ballot measure certified for North Carolina's 2026 general election as of the manifest generation date. Citizens in North Carolina cannot initiate statewide ballot measures — all measures must be referred by the legislature.
